An edge in a hypergraph is defined as a set containing at least two vertices. A vertex set $X$ is considered a minimal vertex set for a specific edge $E$ if $X \subseteq E$, and for every other vertex set $Y$ where $Y \subsetneq E$, the subset $Y$ is not itself an edge. This article addresses two key questions: first, whether there exists a constant $k$ ensuring that every infinite hypergraph includes an infinite collection of these minimal sets, each having a size no greater than $k$; second, assuming $E, F$ are infinite hypergraph edges with a countable difference count ($|E \setminus F| \le \aleph_0$), does there exist an infinite minimal set $X$ for $E$ such that its intersection with $F$ remains infinite ($|X \cap F| = \infty$)? The authors demonstrate that the answer to the first query is negative. Furthermore, they show the premise of this question cannot be satisfied within ZFC by proving it is undecidable.

Ontologies serve as an emerging, formal methodology for modeling domain-specific knowledge, utilizing classes and properties to construct declarative semantic networks. Currently, the predominant tool for visualizing these structures is a layered "treemap," commonly called the mind map. This visualization effectively highlights the taxonomy of nested sub-properties but falls short when dealing with vast quantities of ontological entities and properties. Furthermore, it struggles to represent the non-hierarchical attributes and dense inter-properties that characterize large-scale ontologies. To address these limitations, we introduce OntoPlot, a conceptual visualization framework. This framework offers an innovative approach to displaying ontologies of arbitrary size. By adopting novel rendering strategies for both classes and properties, it enables the effective management of large, complex ontologies.

Automated speech recognition (ASR) utilizing cycle- neural networks has gained significant attention in recent years. While these models have achieved substantial success with large quantities of transcribed speech and audio from diverse domains, they have yet to receive extensive examination regarding their inter-domain characteristics. This study investigates how cycle architectures and inter-domain loss functions can enhance ASR within speech domains that differ linguistically or stylistically from training data. The experiments utilize three extensive corpora representing distinct language domains within Spanish varieties. Our findings reveal that while cyclic models fail to outperform direct transcription methods, the incorporation of inter-domain loss penalties yields significant improvements. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these cycle structures and penalties function synergistically, offering a novel perspective on enhancing cross-domain automatic speech recognition through the integration of cycle architecture and inter-domain optimization.

This paper introduces a fresh navigation strategy for self-regulating robots through an active deduction process. By integrating a high-fidelity environment model with current sensory data, the system generates and evaluates multiple future navigation scenarios. Building upon this navigation framework, we have developed a method for active deduction to address self-regulating robot navigation challenges. Utilizing the inherent knowledge of high-level planners combined with real-time sensory feedback, our approach actively determines subsequent navigation steps by examining both environmental details and task objectives. Unlike traditional methods, our solution goes beyond basic task completion by dynamically assessing environmental conditions to prevent potential hazards such as collisions, falls, or entrapment. Demonstrated through a home-care robot application, our system successfully avoided a fall caused by a deliberately placed ramp, highlighting its efficacy. Building on established research in Computational Grammar and Language Processing, our work introduces a novel approach to Composing Grammar and Language Modeling (CoAptEval) using a transformer-based system. We evaluate the model's performance through two specific metrics: content quality and language model probability. To streamline the assessment process, we employ Auto-Gen, a library designed for automatic goal-oriented conversational agent dialog management. This facilitates the generation of appropriate grammar-specific feedback for each input. To further refine the precision of our evaluation, we integrate GPT-3, a large-scale transformer language model. This allows for the generation of even more granular and specific critiques regarding the quality of the compositional output. This paper details the procedures used in our experimental work using Auto-Gen and GPT-3, as well as the analysis of results obtained through these methods. This framework establishes a baseline for further research and refinement in automatic composition evaluation using transformer-based systems.

Domain-adapted pedestrian identification (DAPEID) addresses identifying individuals across multiple camera views when faces in different domains exhibit significant shifts. While existing methods effectively minimize domain shift to produce consistent features, they often overlook the induced box shift, resulting in increased false positives (FPs) that degrade identification accuracy. This paper introduces Box Reordering, an unsupervised FP reduction framework designed to enhance DAPEID performance. Our approach targets FAs generated by inconsistent cross-domain mappings and exploits the redundancy among such boxes. By identifying and eliminating a majority of these boxes, we locate the true class and reorganize the remaining box per correct match, thereby improving results. Extensive experiments on the two largest multi-view datasets, CPF-147 and CPF1472, demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the current best-in-class approaches. Specifically, on CPF1472, Recall@10 improves by 1.5%, while the False Positive Rate at 10 achieves a reduction of 11.8%.

We introduce an innovative approach to enhancing audio quality by applying distortion effects. Slight deviations in a waveform's timing or phase can produce audibly pleasant auditory alterations. Leveraging the principles of a multiband phaser and ring modulation, we designed a system where the input signal undergoes ring modulation with a sine wave, followed by a timbre-shaping distortion. subsequently, a multiband timbre-bride is applied to the result to create the final output emphasizing both timbral and contrast features. We release our model as an open tool for exploring the intersection of timbral perception and auditory processing in music production.

The kinematic chain is a sequence of kinematically independent kinematic structures, each transferring momentum to the subsequent segment, ultimately releasing an object. In sports, throwing acts as a dynamic control task where athletes impart momentum to an object for a specific aim, relying on a cascade of coordinate transformations. Although throwing techniques are traditionally viewed as highly refined motor skills, our study reveals that even elite throwers can exhibit significant deviation in the object's point of release (POR). We present "FauxThrow," a motion synthesis tool designed to perturb these PORs across a defined spatial range, enabling the evaluation of their effects on various throw metrics. Using this tool, we analyzed data from both amateur and professional users in overhand and sidearm throws. Our findings indicate that simulated errors in the POR have a more profound impact on release velocity than on spin. Furthermore, we observed that while professional throwers demonstrate a marginally lower variance in POR compared to amateurs, both groups exhibit a POR variance large enough to cause substantial variations in object performance. These results underscore the necessity of accurately modeling the release point of momentum objects to achieve a comprehensive understanding of throwing dynamics.

We introduce a novel approach for coupled machine interpretation and parsing, featuring a syntactic-driven, top-down tree generation architecture. In this model, a syntax-aware neural parser constructs the parse tree from the top down, and simultaneously, a system trained to forecast the target interpretation uses the emerging tree structure to generate the final output. Our architecture is trained using end-to-end differential loss, which refines the parser's output based on how the changes in a sentence's derived meaning affect the overall performance score. Experiments conducted on the Parse IAC dataset confirm that our simultaneous approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods relying on input parse trees, yielding a 6.9% relative improvement in sentence classification and a 6.8% relative improvement in syntactic parsing accuracy.

Accurate energy values for molecular binding on astrophysical surfaces are essential to understanding the chemistry within the interstellar medium. Consequently, we have established the Binding Energy Assessment Platform (BEAP) to facilitate binding energy calculations and distribute these values uniformly to researchers. Geometric Brownian motion, commonly used to describe stochastic and multiplicative processes in various domains, features parameters that can be precisely determined from observed data. This study examines a modified geometric Brownian motion that incorporates a lower limit; however, this constraint renders the estimation of its parameters impossible using standard techniques due to the specific nature of the barrier. We propose an alternative, general approach for estimating parameters that is applicable to broader stochastic and multiplicative systems featuring observation-dependent constraints.

This work introduces a novel method for estimating the overlap between an arbitrary quantum state and shalled-out basis states. Specifically, it utilizes random Clifford circuits with shallow depth to compute these estimates. By establishing theoretical bounds regarding both the accuracy and computational efficiency, the study demonstrates that a circuit depth scaling as the polynomial of log(1/δ) is required to attain an overlap approximation within an error margin of δ. Empirical validation through comparisons with various other approximation algorithms confirms the superiority of this proposed approach.

The complex Ginzburg-Landau (CGL) equation, which extends the standard nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger (NLS) equation by incorporating dispersion and nonlinear effects, displays a clear dependence on the reflection coefficient's behavior across all wavenumbers in its linear regime. Specifically, while the inverse scattering transform applies directly to the NLS equation due to the negligible status of linear reflection, this is not the case for CGL equations. This study provides rigorous estimates of the reflection coefficient for the II-class Davey-Stewartson equations, revealing a non-constant behavior dependent on $|k|$. These estimates not only elucidate the distinct characteristics of the $|k|$-dependent reflection coefficient but also highlight the distinct behaviors observed in the large and small $|k|$-wave regimes.

Neural network-aided classification is extensively used across numerous domains, though it is frequently plagued by the need for extensive training datasets and vulnerability to adversarial inputs, which can compromise its reliability. Consequently, this study introduces Sibylvariant, a new family of techniques designed to enhance the resilience of network architectures. These methods leverage a binary classifier to modify incoming data and either reject or accept it. When used to reject data, the classifier prevents the input from reaching the network, whereas if the data is accepted, the system remains unaffected by the alteration. This approach has been evaluated on the Effect of Early-Time Manipulation (EETM) scenario, where an adversary attempts to change incoming text to force a pre-trained classifier into the wrong label. Experimental results demonstrate that Sibylvariant significantly improves the classifier's ability to withstand such attacks.

Recent advancements in resource-constrained environments have enabled the deployment of sophisticated Machine Translation (MT) models across devices with limited computing power. Knowledge distillation and quantization serve as key methodologies to develop efficient, low-power MT architectures. However, despite their widespread adoption, the robustness of these models is frequently overlooked. This paper evaluates the resilience of MT architectures derived from distillation and quantization using a rigorous benchmarking process. Utilizing the OPUS-MT framework, we assess these models' performance across three source languages and five target languages, considering both in-domain and out-of-domain scenarios to identify vulnerabilities. Results indicate that low-resource translated models are highly susceptible to adversarial inputs, with distillation-produced models exhibiting superior robustness relative to those created through quantization. Consequently, quantization and distillation are recommended to enhance adversarial resilience in low-resource settings.

Building upon this foundation, this paper introduces a novel HSVM architecture designed for scenarios involving only one hypergraph. This single-hypergraph Lagrangian-driven SVM (H-Lagr-SVM) operates by utilizing exclusively one massive hypergraph feature alongside traditional graph-based features. This dual-feature approach enables the model to effectively capture characteristics that prior single-factor HSVMs failed to identify. Deep learning approaches in medical image segmentation often demand vast quantities of labeled training data to achieve top-tier performance. In clinical settings like pneumothorax detection, acquiring expert annotations incurs significant time and financial costs, creating barriers to achieving high accuracy without sufficient labeled data. This study investigates whether enhancing training inputs can improve model performance while drastically cutting the number of annotations required. Specifically, we trained a segmentation network using varied image augmentation strategies and evaluated its ability to segrete lung areas from chest X-ray images. We introduced a reduction scheme that minimizes labeled inputs by applying expert knowledge to optimize training efficacy. Our results demonstrate that, compared to a baseline requiring extensive manual labeling, our proposed method requires 75% fewer labeled images while maintaining equivalent segmentation accuracy.

Textual image descriptions generated today tend to be overly verbose, containing numerous unnecessary management words. To create concise and direct descriptions, we present a novel framework called MIVID, which stands for Maintaining Simple Direct Image-Conditioned Language Generation through Prompting. MIVID utilizes multi-task learning to simultaneously optimize three objectives: (1) generating concise text, (2) creating a specialized token to represent this simplicity within the model vocabulary, and (3) expanding the textual boundaries for that simplicity token. This framework is compatible with existing image description generators, requiring no modifications to their pre-trained parameters or architectural structures. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIVID significantly improves textual conciseness compared to current methods, even while achieving comparable or superior image description quality. Furthermore, its proposed simplicity token can effectively boundary simple linguistic expressions for new tasks within the model without additional training.

We present a formalization of the diverse causal theories surrounding "intolerable or unacceptably high risk," and the resulting damage or badness of outcomes. Our approach unifies and expands existing literature by unifying the following key insights: the use of comparative probabilities to define risk; the specific claim that out-of-control risks are unacceptable regardless of their severity; and the specific claim that in-control risks may still be acceptable if their severity is sufficiently low. Our framework demonstrates that the first three positions—each distinct in their reasoning about damage—also align with the first four standard ethical positions on permissible risk. Our approach clarifies the relationships between these various positions and the reasons underlying their differences.

Although deep learning has become a vital tool across various disciplines, deploying and expanding these models in real-world scenarios remains difficult. Current research often overlooks their distribution characteristics and inherent learning capabilities. To address this gap, we introduce MMLSpark, a framework designed for large-scale deep learning deployment and retraining on distributed systems. This system supports dynamic model updates and new data ingestion directly within production environments without requiring complete model redesign. By leveraging the Apache Spark ecosystem, we achieve performance that matches or surpasses current state-of-the-art solutions. We have validated the framework's real-world utility by deploying and continuously monitoring two object detection models, as well as a face recognition model, across a wide range of new and unseen data sets.

Voice interpretation involves using speech recognition (ASR) and speech translation (ST) to convert spoken words into target language text. Typically, ASR and ST are trained using audio from their respective source languages, a limitation that hinders their effectiveness when processing speech from unknown, zero-shot languages. In such scenarios, ASR fails to accurately recognize phonological details and word boundaries, which in turn compromises ST's ability to generate correct translations. To address this, we introduce a data-efficient approach for generating intermediate aligned bilingual sentence drafts. This draft generation is based on extracting and aligning sentence-level monolingual translations across languages. By comparing the shared syntactic structures, word order similarities help pinpoint corresponding phrases to establish aligned sentence pairs. These alignments serve as constraints to refine the input to standard ST models, resulting in improved intermediate bilingual drafts. Consequently, these drafts provide more accurate guidance to ST models, enhancing overall zero-shot voice interpretation. Experiments on four language pairs confirm that our method significantly boosts zero-shot voice interpretation performance.

We introduce thermal analogues of the Coleman-Gurtin model within the framework of generalized thermodynamics, developed specifically to address scenarios where active boundary conditions are required. These conditions arise in the study of insulating materials subjected to intense external heat fluxes. We demonstrate that our formulated system adheres strictly to the classical balance equations and the Coleman-Holtzmann inequality while demonstrating flexibility in handling diverse forms of internal dissipation. Furthermore, we explore the theoretical foundation for several recent variations found in the literature, presenting their corresponding density functions capable of yielding these specific models through variational methods.

A primary challenge in integrating renewable sources lies in the unpredictable fluctuations of generation capacity, which can cause grid instability during peak production. While energy exchange TSOs and distribution system operators (DSOs) must forecast load and generation profiles, short-term predictions are critical for managing the low-voltage grid (LV-GRID)—specifically its transformers and cables—to prevent overloads, with a specific emphasis on daily peak loads. This research introduces a machine learning framework combining forecasts from multiple models using a probabilistic load prediction system. The study utilizes the 2018 German "Grid4You" dataset to train models on both daily peak demand and annual full-year profiles. The results indicate that while the models achieve state-of-the-art performance in estimating daily profiles, combining forecasts yields significant improvements specifically regarding the prediction of daily maximum loads.

We introduce a structured framework for merging field-specific knowledge with machine learning models, beginning with a taxonomy of five knowledge categories derived from current literature. Following this, we develop a typology utilizing data from Reddit communities in various domains to identify challenges ML engineers face when dealing with non-technical domain expertise. Lastly, we propose a blueprint, offering guidance for effectively incorporating such knowledge into machine learning practices.

Although deep learning has produced significant advancements in vertebral localization and classification within medical imaging, its application is often hindered by the challenges posed by complex backgrounds and the high variability of vertebral poses and levels. Consequently, neural networks struggle to extract robust features from these irregular inputs. To address this, we introduce a framework for enhancing and standardizing vertebral structures in CT scans, thereby improving the representation of key features. This proposed system integrates two core components: a novel vertebrae-aware enhancement network designed to correct misalignments in 3D CT volumes, and a boundary refinement module that leverages human anatomical knowledge to further improve enhancement precision. Experimental evaluations indicate that this enhancement framework substantially boosts the performance of subsequent localization and recognition models specifically designed for 3D CT data.

We investigate the conditions under which bound states of an electron in a cavity remain stable against electron-positron pair production. This analysis builds upon our earlier work regarding the stationary states of a charged particle in an external field, which demonstrated that stable eigenstates can emerge if the charge oscillates perpendicularly to the electric field. Specifically, this dynamic stability is linked to the absence of resonant enhancement in the imaginary component of the complex scattering energy for the bound electron. We further demonstrate that when the electron's oscillation frequency aligns resonantly with an emerging bound state, the resulting scattering process can dynamically stabilize this state, even extending to the scenario where the bound state originates from an initially unconfined (free) electron. This dynamic stability relies on suppressed tunneling to the Cerenkov radiation continuum, thereby inhibiting pair production. Our numerical findings indicate that stable frequencies can be realized in the experimentally accessible interaction regime, contingent upon generating bound states through the dynamic trapping of a free electron via laser fields.

While electric actuator technology has enabled quadruped robots to master complex locomotion, assembling these high-fidelity, high-cost components limits deployment to well-defined environments. Conversely, the availability and affordability of actuation technology have spurred a need for efficient, sustainable robotics solutions. This research investigates quadruped locomotion by focusing on the effective use of elastic actuators. Through the simulation of learned open-loop gaits in the PyBullet environment using a Pytorch optimizer, the study produces an open-loop strategy that allows the learned gaits to vary joint velocities and torque patterns, thereby creating varied joint velocity profiles that are not uniform across all joints. Finally, the study demonstrates the viability of these learned elastic open-loop gaits on a real-world robot platform.

This paper explores the issue of divisibility raised by boundary interaction in diverse quantum systems. It introduces a variational approach to determine the annihilation operator optimal divisibility states and offers insights into their characteristics and properties. Furthermore, it proposes a method for calculating these states and demonstrates their application in calculating the expectation value of the position operator within the ground state.

Magnetic reconnection is essential to numerous astrophysical and plasma processes, driving phenomena ranging from solar flares, coronal loops, and magnetic islands to geomagnetic substorms. Although extensively studied, the physics of tearing modes in slab plasmas at mini-scale and collisionless conditions remains complex. This paper examines the growth rate, magnetic islands' evolution, and the influence of key factors, including plasma temperature and magnetic shear. Specifically, the impact of the Hall effect on mode development is explored, revealing that island expansion transitions from scaling with $\tau \sim S^{1/3}$ to $\sim S^{1/2}$ as collisionality increases from high levels down to experimentally achievable values. Furthermore, the evolution of $j_y$ and $j_z$ components of the current is linked to the observed growth rate variations. The analysis also considers the impact of pressure gradients, showing that the pressure gradient can either suppress or enhance growth depending on slab parameters, while demonstrating that the physics of these tearing modes remains largely independent of whether collisions dominate.

Feature-level trait manipulation (LTM) is a recently introduced approach designed to modify specific attributes within images. Although it has shown promise for improving fashion image retrieval (FIR) and fashion product retrieval (FPR)—two fields that rely on intra-garment style variance and inter-brand consistency—current FIR and FPR methods utilizing LTM face two primary limitations. First, they often fail to achieve optimal results because the latent traits are not derived from a well-trained encoder. Second, they utilize a suboptimal loss function that uses manual human ratings rather than explicit labels, resulting in subpar performance.

To address these limitations, we present an advanced FIR and FPR framework based on LGM that replaces the standard encoding architecture with a discriminative one. This new model is trained using a loss function explicitly optimized for LGM, rather than relying solely on subjective ratings. Additionally, we introduce a novel pre-training strategy that leverages task-irrelevant data to enhance LGM's ability. Our experimental results indicate that this approach significantly outperforms the original LGM design, as well as current FIR and FPR state-of-the-art methods on established datasets.

Light field imaging captures multi-view data from a scene, and one of its primary advantages is its capacity to render three-dimensional (3D) depth maps. However, traditional single-to-single pixel depth generation methods are often inadequate because they fail to account for local occlusions, resulting in depth inaccuracies within these unobservable or occluded areas. This study introduces a learning framework that utilizes machine learning to enhance the estimation of occluded regions by integrating contextual and geometric cues. Specifically, our model predicts pixel offsets relative to the main view to construct a more precise composite image, thereby serving as a robust proxy for depth estimation. At the core of our approach lies a novel algorithm called the Occlusion-Responsive Expense Creator (OREC). This component functions as a surrogate system that forecasts geometric offsets, effectively reducing reliance on detailed occlusion masks. Extensive experiments conducted on four real-light field datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves superior accuracy compared to existing methods, marking a significant advancement in how such techniques address occlusion challenges.

The proliferation of wireless devices has significantly impacted home Wi-Fi networks, often degrading network performance due to suboptical Access Point (AP) placement and signal relaying strategies. This paper introduces a Access Point selection algorithm designed to choose the AP with the least channel load, utilizing IEEE 802.11k/v protocols. Furthermore, we present a novel Extender selection algorithm that directs clients to the Extender with the strongest link rather than relying on conventional methods based on received signal strength indicator (RSSI). Our proposed system demonstrates that selecting the least-loaded AP outstrips the performance of the home's primary AP, while the new Extender selection method outperforms existing solutions.
